title: Best Mac 2026: Every Apple Mac and MacBook compared
content:
Macworld

Choosing the best Mac in 2026 means finding the right combination of performance, features and price for the way you work. Whether you’re buying your first Mac, replacing an older computer or looking for more power, this guide will help you understand your options and choose with confidence.

Do you need a laptop to carry around or a desktop for a permanent workspace? Which processor will handle your apps, how much memory and storage should you buy, and which connections do you need? We explain what these differences mean in practice, helping you identify the features worth paying for.

We also help you work out the total cost. Memory and storage upgrades can significantly increase the price, while some models require a separate display and accessories. Our configuration advice and retailer price comparisons will help you balance your needs against your budget and decide where to spend – or save.

Below, you’ll find our recommendations followed by detailed explanations of every current Mac family, including their strengths, limitations and upgrade options. Together, these will help you narrow your shortlist and choose the right Mac for your work, home or studies. For a closer look at Apple’s laptops, see our MacBook comparison.

Best Mac 2026: Mac & MacBook Buyers Guide

The MacBook Air is our top Mac for most people in 2026, offering an excellent balance of performance, portability, battery life, and value. For tighter budgets, the MacBook Neo starts at $699/£699 and is Apple’s most affordable laptop.

For demanding creative and professional work, choose the MacBook Pro. The touchscreen MacBook Pro adds the flexibility to interact directly with the display alongside the keyboard and trackpad.

If you don’t need portability, the Mac mini, starting at $899/£899, offers good value if you already own a display and accessories. The iMac combines the computer and display in an all-in-one design that’s ideal for the home, while the Mac Studio provides greater power for intensive creative work and AI development.

What is it? The 13-inch MacBook Air is Apple’s thin and light laptop for everyday use, offering more performance and features than the cheaper MacBook Neo.

What’s new? Apple introduced the M5 MacBook Air in March 2026, featuring the M5 chip with its faster CPU and GPU. The base configuration now starts with 512GB of storage (double the previous model), along with faster SSD speeds, more memory bandwidth, and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

Who’s it for? It’s perfect for students and everyday users who want a lightweight laptop that’s easy to carry, and powerful enough for working, studying, browsing, and doing light creative work. If you want a larger screen there is a 15-inch MacBook Air, which we discuss below.

How much does the 13-inch MacBook Air cost? The entry-level 13-inch M5 MacBook Air costs from $1,299/£1,299, that’s up $200/£200 from the launch price of $1,099/£1,099. You can create build-to-order models with more memory (up to 32GB) or storage (up to 4TB).

What are the specifications? The standard specs for the M5 MacBook Air offer an improvement compared to the previous generation. The MacBook Air now ships with 512GB SSD as standard.

  • Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports: $1,299/£1,299.
  • Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports: $1,399/£1,399.
  • Additional options: Up to 32GB memory, 4TB storage.

What are display specifications?

  • While referred to as 13-inch, when measured diagonally the screen is 13.6-inches.
  • The 13.6-inch Liquid Retina on the M5 MacBook Air display has a native resolution of 2,560×1,664 and 500 nits brightness.
  • The MacBook Air M5 can support two external displays.

How do I connect stuff? The M5 MacBook Air models supports Thunderbolt 4, which means that they can support a dual monitor set up. If you want to connect USB-A devices, you need either a USB-C to USB-A adapter, like Apple’s $19 / £19 one, or a USB-C hub that has USB-A ports. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately. See our round-up of the best USB-C hubs and adapters.

The 2026 MacBook Air offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) for connecting to a network. It also provides built-in Bluetooth (6) for wirelessly connecting a mouse or other peripherals. If you want to connect to an ethernet network, you need an adapter.

How fast is it? In our tests the M5 saw consistent gains over the M4 in the previous generation, as you can see in our Mac processor benchmarks. In some benchmarks the M5 even beats the M1 Ultra. If you are upgrading from an old Mac – especially if it is one with an Intel chip – you will see a huge difference.

Any other considerations? The MacBook Air is more than fast enough for everyday use and occasional creative work. Its fanless design keeps it silent, but performance can drop during sustained demanding tasks as it reduces speed to control heat. If you regularly run lengthy video exports, large code builds or other intensive workloads, a MacBook Pro with active cooling is a better choice. Memory and internal storage cannot be upgraded after purchase, so choose a configuration that meets your likely longer-term needs. Prioritize enough memory for your apps; you can add storage later with an external SSD. The Air still uses M5, while Apple now offers M6 versions of the standard MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini. An M6 MacBook Air could follow in spring 2027. If you need a new laptop now, the M5 Air remains a capable option, particularly at a discount.

Why we recommend the 13-inch MacBook Air: The MacBook Air is a great choice for someone who does general-purpose work and moves around a lot, such as a student or a self-employed person.

We compare the MacBook Air vs MacBook Pro separately.

What’s new? The MacBook Neo is Apple’s new entry-level Mac laptop. It’s powered by an iPhone-class chip (the A18 Pro) rather than an M-series processor, and it introduces a colorful design and a simplified feature set at a much lower starting price, although not as low as it was, thanks to Apple’s June 2026 price hikes which pushed prices up $100.

Who’s it for? The MacBook Neo is designed to appeal to students and those who want to use a laptop for everyday tasks like web browsing, video calls, schoolwork, streaming, email and office apps. Because it uses an A18 Pro iPhone chip and is limited to 8GB of non-upgradable RAM, it is not suitable for heavy video editing or large-scale photo processing.

How much does the MacBook Neo cost? At launch the MacBook Neo was the cheapest Mac laptop Apple has ever released, starting at $599/£599. That price is now slightly more, at $699/£699, but it’s still about half the price of a MacBook Air.

What are the specifications? The MacBook Neo is the first Mac to use an A-series processor, the same family used in iPhones. That chip has a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU, 8GB unified memory, and either 256GB or 512GB storage.

  • Apple A18 Pro, 6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, 8GB memory, 256GB SSD, two USB-C ports: $699/£699.
  • Apple A18 Pro, 6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, 8GB memory, 512GB SSD, two USB-C ports: $799/£799.
  • Additional options: None.

What are display specifications? The MacBook Neo features a 13-inch Liquid Retina display with 2,408×1,506 resolution at 220 ppi, at up to 500 nits and sRGB color. That should be good enough for everyday work.

How do I connect stuff? Connectivity is basic. There are two USB-C ports; one is USB 3, the other is slower USB 2. There isn’t a separate MagSafe port so charging is via USB-C. There is a 3.5mm headphone jack. Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 6 are included.

How fast is it? MacBook Neo uses the A18 Pro chip that first appeared in the iPhone 16 Pro. Our tests and benchmarks of that chip indicate that it offers similar performance to the M1. It is suitable for everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming, and office apps.

Any other considerations? The MacBook Neo’s low price comes with several trade-offs: there’s no Thunderbolt, MagSafe charging or backlit keyboard, and Touch ID is available only on the 512GB model. Unified memory is limited to 8GB and cannot be upgraded, so consider whether that will meet your longer-term needs before buying. The Neo uses the A18 Pro chip. A refresh with a newer, more powerful processor could arrive in 2027.

Why we recommend the MacBook Neo: This is the most affordable way to own a Mac laptop – unless you buy a used or refurbished model. If you don’t need pro-level performance it’s a very compelling entry-point into Apple’s ecosystem.

What is it? The 15-inch MacBook Air is essentially identical to the 13-inch model above aside from the bigger screen and six-speaker system rather than four speakers. Surprisingly, battery life isn’t better on the 15-inch, despite the bigger battery.

What’s new? The M5 MacBook Air arrived in March 2026. Like the 13-inch version it features the M5 chip for faster CPU and GPU performance compared to the previous generation. The base configuration now starts with 512GB of storage (double the previous model), along with faster SSD speeds, more memory bandwidth, and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

Who’s it for? The 15-inch MacBook Air is ideal for anyone who wants a big-screen laptop for far less than the price of a 14-inch or 16-inch MacBook Pro. The big screen will allow more room for spreadsheets and browser tabs, and for multitasking with multiple apps open. It’s also great choice for anyone who values portability due to its lightweight and thin design.

How much does the 15-inch MacBook Air cost? The price of the 15-inch model was $1,299/£1,299, but following the June 2026 price increases it now starts at $1,499/£1,499. There are three configurations and you can create build-to-order models with up to 32GB memory and 4TB storage.

What are the specifications? The specifications of the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air are generally the same as the 13-inch model, except there is no 8-core GPU option here. The actual screen measurements, measured diagonally are 15.3in. You are essentially paying $200/£200 more for the bigger screen.

  • Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 512GB SSD, two Thunderbolt 4 ports: $1,499/£1,499.
  • Additional options: Up to 32GB memory, 4TB storage.

What are display specifications?

  • While referred to as 15-inch, when measured diagonally the screen is 15.3-inches.
  • The 15.3-inch Liquid Retina display has a native resolution of 2,880×1,864 and 500 nits brightness.
  • The MacBook Air M5 can support two external displays.

How do I connect stuff? Both M5 MacBook Air models support Thunderbolt 4 and can support a dual monitor set up. For USB-A devices you need a USB-C to USB adapter (Apple sells one for $19 / £19), or a USB-C hub with USB-A ports. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately. See our round-up of the best USB-C hubs and adapters.

The 2026 MacBook Air offers the new standards of Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth (6). If you want to connect to an ethernet network, you need an adapter.

How fast is it? This is the same M5 as found in the 14-inch MacBook Pro, so you can expect similar performance. In our tests we found the M5 to be faster than the M1 Ultra in some benchmarks. If you are updating from an older Mac expect a big boost.

Any other considerations? The Air doesn’t have a fan to keep the computer cool, so it may throttle down its speed during long processing sessions, such as video editing or compiling code. If that’s the kind of work you intend to do, a MacBook Pro would be a better option. Also note that you won’t be able to update RAM or storage later, so get as much as you can afford. The Air still uses the M5 chip, while Apple now offers M6 versions of the standard MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac mini. An M6 MacBook Air could follow in spring 2027.

Why we recommend the 15-inch MacBook Air: Starting at $1,499/£1,499, the 15-inch MacBook Air is a much more affordable Mac laptop than the 14-inch MacBook Pro, which starts at $1,999/£1,999, so if you want your screen to be bigger than 13 inches, and you don’t need the power of a MacBook Pro for the kind of work you do, the 15-inch MacBook Air is a great option.

What is it? The 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro is the entry-level model in Apple’s professional laptop range. It combines a standard M6 chip with active cooling, a Liquid Retina XDR display and more ports than the MacBook Air. More powerful M5 Pro and M5 Max models remain available, including separate OLED touchscreen versions. The M6 model retains a conventional, non-touchscreen display.

What’s new? Announced on October 27, 2026, the M6 model replaces M5 with a 2nm processor featuring a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, up from 10 cores each. It also gains a dual 16-core Neural Engine, Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. The enclosure, display, memory capacities and storage options remain largely unchanged.

Who’s it for? The M6 MacBook Pro suits users who want a better display, additional connections and more sustained processing power than the MacBook Air offers. Its cooling fan makes it better suited to lengthy video exports, code builds and other demanding tasks. For heavier graphics workloads or projects requiring more than 32GB of memory, consider M5 Pro or M5 Max instead.

How much does the 14-inch MacBook Pro cost? The M6 model starts at $1,999/£1,999 with 16GB of unified memory and a 1TB SSD. That matches the outgoing M5 model’s most recent starting price, rather than its lower original launch price.

What are the specifications?

  • Apple M6 with a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU and dual 16-core Neural Engine.
  • 16GB unified memory and a 1TB SSD as standard. Optional 24GB or 32GB memory and 2TB or 4TB storage.
  • Memory bandwidth of 153GB/s with 16GB, rising to 170GB/s with 24GB or 32GB.
  • Apple rates battery life at up to 24 hours of video streaming or 16 hours of wireless web browsing.

What are the display specifications?

  • 14.2-inch mini-LED Liquid Retina XDR display with a resolution of 3024 × 1964.
  • Up to 1,000 nits sustained full-screen HDR brightness and 1,600 nits peak HDR brightness.
  • Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness outdoors.
  • ProMotion adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz, P3 wide color and True Tone.
  • Optional nano-texture glass.
  • A notch housing a 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View support.

How do I connect stuff? There are three Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe 3 charging and a headphone jack. You may need an adapter for older accessories; see our MacBook adapter guide. The M6 supports two external displays alongside its built-in screen. Wireless connectivity improves to Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, replacing the previous generation’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. In the U.S., a 70W USB-C adapter is included. Buyers in the U.K. and Europe need to supply a compatible adapter separately. Fast charging requires a 96W or higher USB Power Delivery source.

How fast is it? Apple claims up to 30 percent faster graphics and 25 percent faster on-device AI workloads than M5. We’ll run independent testing to establish the gains in everyday apps and sustained workloads. The newer M6 name also doesn’t mean it is superior to the M5 Pro or M5 Max, which offer more CPU and GPU cores, greater memory bandwidth and higher memory capacities.

Any other considerations? Memory and internal storage cannot be upgraded after purchase. Choose enough memory for your likely longer-term needs; external SSDs can provide additional storage later. If you want OLED or touchscreen input, you’ll need a PROLED XDR model.

Why we recommend the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6): It offers a useful middle ground between the MacBook Air and the more expensive Pro and Max models. You get a brighter HDR display with ProMotion, additional ports, active cooling and Apple’s latest standard M-series processor. Compare prices with the Air after matching memory and storage: the Pro’s premium is worth considering if those features will improve your work, while the Air remains lighter and more affordable.

What is it? The 14-inch MacBook Pro can also be configured with an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip, which are much more powerful than the standard chip in the M6 MacBook Pro. The Pro and Max MacBook Pro can support up to 18-core CPU, 40-core GPU, 128GB memory and 8TB storage, for a seriously fast Mac laptop. There’s a larger 16-inch MacBook Pro with similar specs that we discuss below. These models retain mini-LED Liquid Retina XDR displays. Apple also offers separate PROLED XDR versions with OLED touchscreens, discussed below.

What’s new? The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max was introduced in March 2026 and introduces Apple’s new Fusion Architecture chip that combines two 3nm CPU and GPU dies into a single unified system on a chip, which lets Apple scale performance and efficiency. In addition, the GPU includes a Neural Accelerator in every core, which Apple claims delivers up to 4x the AI performance of the previous generation. There is also faster memory and faster SSD speeds. In October 2026 touchscreen versions of these MacBooks joined the range.

Who’s it for? If your work demands serious processing power, these machines are built to handle it. If you regularly work in professional software, the 14-inch MacBook Pro is a strong choice, and with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip they’re the most powerful laptops Apple has ever made. The 14-inch model costs less than the 16-inch version, making it the more budget-friendly option, and if you use an external monitor the screen size matters less. The M5 Pro MacBook Pro is designed for demanding professional tasks like software development, managing large photo libraries, or editing 4K video, while the M5 Max is aimed at even heavier workflows such as 3D animation, complex simulations, AI development, and high-end video production. These versions suit buyers who want Pro/Max performance without paying for OLED and touch.

How much does the 14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro & Max cost? The price now starts at $2,499/£2,499 (up from $2,199/£2,199) for the M5 Pro. The M5 Max version starts at $4,099/£4,099, up from $3,599/£3,599 prior to June 2026, and a gigantic leap from the previous generation starting price of $3,199/£3,199 (that M4 Max model came with 1TB SSD rather than 2TB).

What are the specifications? Here are the standard configurations for the 14-inch MacBook Pro.

  • Apple M5 Pro, 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB memory, 1TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $2,499/£2,499.
  • Apple M5 Pro, 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU, 24GB memory, 1TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $2,699/£2,699.
  • Apple M5 Max, 18-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 36GB memory, 2TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $4,099/£4,099.
  • Apple M5 Max, 18-core CPU, 40-core GPU, 48GB memory, 2TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $4,699/£4,699.
  • M5 Pro upgrade options: Up to 64GB unified memory and 4TB SSD storage.
  • M5 Max upgrade options: Up to 128GB unified memory and 8TB SSD storage. The 128GB memory option requires the 40-core GPU configuration.
  • Display option: Nano-texture glass is available at an additional cost.

What are display specifications?

  • Apple refers to it as a 14-inch screen, but the screen measures 14.2-inches.
  • The 14.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display has a resolution of 3024 × 1964 at 254 pixels per inch. It offers 1,000 nits sustained full-screen HDR brightness, 1,600 nits peak HDR brightness and up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness outdoors. It also supports a 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio and ProMotion adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz.
  • The notch at the top of the display conceals the 12MP Center Stage camera with support for Desk View and 1080p HD video recording. The notch does not affect the available screen area—the work area is a 16-by-10 space, while the screen surrounding the notch is considered extra space and is used to display the menu bar.

How do I connect stuff? The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and Max offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6 for wireless connectivity. There are three Thunderbolt 5/USB C ports, an SDXC slot for plugging in memory cards from cameras, audio recorders, and other devices, and an HDMI port for connecting an external display or projector (the HDMI port supports multichannel audio output). In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately.

How fast is it? Apple built the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models with pro users in mind and it shows in the performance. With the M5 Pro and M5 Max you can enjoy the fastest Mac laptops Apple has ever made. M5 Max offers more GPU resources and greater memory bandwidth, but the benefit depends on your applications and workload.

Any other considerations? The MacBook Pro models with M5 Pro chips cost significantly more than other Macs, and the Max version costs even more, so you should consider whether the extra performance will actually benefit your workflow.

Why we recommend the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max): These models offer the same processor and memory options as the touchscreen versions at lower starting prices. They are particularly worth considering if you work mainly with an external display or prefer keyboard and trackpad input. Choose the PROLED XDR version if its OLED screen, touch controls and reduced weight justify the extra cost for your work.

What is it? Officially called the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, this is Apple’s first touchscreen Mac laptop. It offers the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip options as the non-touchscreen models above, paired with a tandem OLED display and a smaller, lighter enclosure. The keyboard and trackpad remain, with touch providing another way to interact with your Mac.

What’s new? Announced on October 28, 2026, the touchscreen model introduces Dynamic Island, higher peak display brightness, Adobe RGB support and a redesigned hinge. The 14-inch versions weigh 1.38kg with M5 Pro or 1.40kg with M5 Max – 220g lighter than their non-touch equivalents. Other changes include camera stabilization, redesigned speakers and a 16TB storage option for M5 Max.

Who’s it for? Consider this version if you want Pro-level processing power and regularly work on the laptop’s own screen. Photographers, designers and video editors may value the OLED display and expanded color support, while touch offers direct scrolling, zooming and manipulation of content. If you mainly use an external monitor, the less expensive non-touchscreen model may offer better value.

How much does it cost? The 14-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899/£2,899 with M5 Pro, or $4,499/£4,499 with M5 Max. Those starting prices are $400/£400 above the equivalent non-touchscreen versions.

What are the specifications? Processor and memory options match the non-touchscreen models:

  • M5 Pro: Starts with a 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB memory and 1TB SSD. Available with an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU, up to 64GB memory and up to 4TB storage.
  • M5 Max: Starts with an 18-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 36GB memory and 2TB SSD. The 40-core GPU configuration supports up to 128GB memory. Both Max versions offer storage up to 16TB.
  • Apple rates video-streaming battery life at up to 22 hours with M5 Pro or 20 hours with M5 Max, matching the non-touch models.

What are the display specifications?

  • 14.2-inch tandem OLED PROLED XDR touchscreen, with a resolution of 3024 × 1986.
  • Up to 1,000 nits sustained full-screen brightness, with 2,000 nits peak HDR and peak outdoor SDR brightness.
  • ProMotion adaptive refresh rates from 10Hz to 120Hz.
  • P3 and Adobe RGB color support, plus True Tone.
  • Dynamic Island replaces the notch.
  • Standard antireflective glass or an optional nano-texture finish.

How do I connect stuff? Connections are familiar: three Thunderbolt 5 USB-C ports, HDMI, SDXC, MagSafe 3 and a headphone jack, alongside Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. M5 Pro supports up to three external displays; M5 Max supports up to four.

How fast is it? The touchscreen models use the same processors, core configurations and memory bandwidth as their non-touch equivalents. The $400 premium buys display and design improvements rather than a newer chip generation. We’ll be conducting tests to establish whether the redesigned cooling affects sustained performance.

Any other considerations? Touch complements the keyboard and trackpad, but its usefulness will depend on your apps and working habits. Before paying extra, look for reviews covering touch ergonomics, fingerprints, reflections and app support. Memory and internal storage cannot be upgraded later, so choose your configuration around your expected workload.

Why we recommend the 14-inch touchscreen MacBook Pro: It combines professional processing options with OLED, direct touchscreen input and a more portable design. It is worth considering if those improvements will benefit your everyday work. Choose the non-touchscreen version if you want the same processor and memory options at a lower price.

What is it? The 16-inch MacBook Pro offers a similar set of specs and configuration options as the 14-inch MacBook Pro (above), but it has a higher price, a bigger screen, and better battery life – 24 vs 22 hours from the 14-inch model.

What’s new? Like the 14-inch MacBook Pro discussed above, the 16-inch MacBook Pro features Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, which use Apple’s Fusion Architecture to combine two 3-nm CPU and GPU dies into a single unified system on a chip. This design allows Apple to scale both performance and efficiency. The GPU also includes a Neural Accelerator in every core, which Apple says means it can deliver up to four times the AI performance of the previous generation. There is also faster memory and improved SSD speeds compared to the previous generation.

Who’s it for? This is Apple’s largest ‘pro’ laptop and it’s designed for people who need a portable Mac to do work that demands extreme processing power. You could save some money with the 14-inch MacBook Pro, but if you need a big screen on your laptop this is the Mac for you. You’ll also benefit from longer battery life. Configured with the M5 Max this is the fastest and most powerful laptop Apple has ever created.

How much does the 16-inch MacBook Pro cost? There are three standard configurations starting at $2,999/£2,999 (up from $2,699/£2,699, which was already $200/£200 more than the previous generation, although with double the storage). The ultimate option is a $4,999/£4,999 (up from $4,399/£4,399) for a M5 Max.

What are the specifications? Here are the standard configurations for the 16-inch MacBook Pro introduced in 2026. The screen measures 16.2in diagonally.

  • Apple M5 Pro, 18-core CPU, 20-core GPU, 24GB memory, 1TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $2,999/£2,999 (up from $2,699/£2,699).
  • Apple M5 Max, 18-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 36GB memory, 2TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $4,399/£4,399 (up from $3,899/£3,899).
  • Apple M5 Max, 18-core CPU, 40-core GPU, 48GB memory, 2TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $4,999/£4,999. (up from $4,399/£4,399).
  • Additional options: Up to 64GB memory and 4TB storage with M5 Pro; up to 128GB memory and 8TB storage with M5 Max. Optional nano-texture display.

What are display specifications?

  • When measured diagonally, the screen is 16.2-inches.
  • The 16.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display has a native resolution of 3,456×2,234, 1,600 nits of maximum brightness, and 1,000 nits for HDR content, but it now offers 1000 nits for standard content, up from 600. You’ll also get a 1,000,000-to-1 contrast ratio and ProMotion support with a variable refresh rate of up to 120Hz.
  • The notch at the top of the display conceals the 12MP Center Stage camera with support for Desk View and 1080p HD video recording. The notch does not affect the available screen area—the work area is a 16-by-10 space, while the screen surrounding the notch is considered extra space and is used to display the menu bar.

How do I connect stuff? The 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and Max offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6 for wireless connectivity. There are three Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports that are compatible with USB-C. If you have wired devices that aren’t USB-C or are an older version of Thunderbolt, you’ll need an adapter. How do I connect stuff? The entry-level iMac has two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports; the higher model has four. Both include a headphone jack, but USB-A accessories require an adapter or a suitable hub or dock. Wireless connectivity improves to Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, replacing Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 on the previous generation. The four-port model includes 2.5Gb Ethernet, while it is an optional upgrade on the two-port version. You’ll need compatible network equipment to benefit from the faster Ethernet connection. The two-port model supports one external display, while the four-port version supports up to two, alongside the built-in screen.

How fast is it?: Apple claims up to 1.5 times faster performance in productivity tasks such as Excel, twice the graphics performance in selected workloads, and five times faster local AI prompt processing than M4. These figures describe Apple’s specified tests, rather than universal improvements across every app. Independent testing is needed to establish real-world gains and sustained performance. The four-port model’s additional CPU and GPU cores give it more processing resources than the entry-level version.

Any other considerations? The base 256GB SSD is restrictive if you keep large photo libraries, videos or games locally. Consider 512GB or more, or budget for an external SSD. Memory cannot be upgraded later, so choose enough for your likely longer-term needs. Compare the complete setup cost with a Mac mini plus a suitable display and accessories. The iMac’s integrated design is convenient, but a separate computer and monitor offer more flexibility when upgrading.

Why we recommend the iMac (M6): It’s a straightforward way to buy a complete Mac desktop with a sharp display, camera, good speakers and matching accessories. For buyers who need its additional features, the $1,699/£1,699 four-port model is worth the extra $200/£200: it adds more CPU and GPU cores, two additional ports, a Touch ID keyboard and included Ethernet, plus higher memory and storage limits. The two-port version remains sufficient for lighter everyday use.

FAQ

1.

What’s best, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro?

We explore this question in detail in our MacBook Air vs MacBook Pro comparison. The MacBook Air is the best choice for most people, offering enough performance for everyday work, studying and many creative tasks. The MacBook Pro is worth considering if you need sustained performance for demanding workloads, more ports or a more advanced display.

The entry-level MacBook Air costs $1,299/£1,299, although you can often spend less by shopping around – we regularly round up the best MacBook Air deals. If you want more screen space without paying for professional-level performance, the 15-inch MacBook Air is considerably cheaper than a 14-inch MacBook Pro.

Within the MacBook Pro range, the standard 14-inch M6 model provides a middle ground between the Air and the more expensive M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations. Its fan helps maintain performance during longer processing tasks, while its Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI port and SDXC card slot add flexibility.

The M5 Pro and M5 Max models suit more demanding professional workloads, offering more CPU and GPU cores, higher memory capacities and Thunderbolt 5. M5 Pro is a strong option for software development, photography and video editing. Consider M5 Max if your work benefits from its additional graphics power, media engines or higher memory ceiling; spending more won’t necessarily make everyday tasks noticeably faster.

You can also choose a MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR touchscreen. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, these models add an OLED display, touch controls alongside the keyboard and trackpad, Dynamic Island, and a thinner, lighter design. Starting at $2,899/£2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399/£3,399 for the 16-inch, they cost $400/£400 more than equivalent non-touch M5 Pro models. They use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families, so the main reasons to pay extra are the display, portability and touch input.

Choosing between a 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro comes down to workspace, portability, battery life and price. The larger model gives you more room for editing timelines, coding and multitasking, while the 14-inch is easier to carry. Both sizes offer powerful Pro and Max configurations. For external monitors, current M5 Pro models support up to three displays and M5 Max models support up to four, depending on resolution and refresh rate.

For a tighter budget, the MacBook Neo lowers the starting price of a Mac laptop to $699/£699. It’s worth comparing its compromises with a discounted previous-generation MacBook Air before deciding.

2.

Should I upgrade from my Intel Mac?

Yes. It’s time! We are now more than six years into Apple’s transition from Intel processors to its own silicon that includes CPU, GPU, and unified memory. The transition began with the introduction of the M1 in November 2020. Since June 2023 every Mac Apple sells uses Apple’s own chips rather than Intel processors.

If you’ve yet to upgrade your Intel Mac to one powered by Apple’s silicon what are you waiting for? If you are concerned that a must-have app doesn’t run on an M-series Mac, consider finding a new app because the performance gains are tremendous.

Another good reason to replace an Intel Mac is that Apple’s support for these models is winding down. macOS Golden Gate, released in September 2026, is the first major version of macOS to support no Intel Macs. Intel Macs compatible with older versions of macOS may continue receiving security updates for a limited period, but they are now outside Apple’s current feature-release cycle. Apple does not guarantee how long those updates will continue, and machines limited to macOS Sequoia are likely to lose support sooner than those capable of running macOS Tahoe. Read: How long does Apple support Macs.

4.

What specs do I really need for my Mac?

Chip: The specs you need depend on what you plan to do with your Mac. For web browsing, email, office apps and light photo editing, a standard M-series chip is more than sufficient. The M6 is available in the Mac mini, iMac and standard 14-inch MacBook Pro, while the MacBook Air uses M5. The budget MacBook Neo uses an A18 Pro chip. A newer generation number doesn’t automatically make a chip better for every workload: compare its CPU, GPU, memory and capabilities with what your apps actually need.

If you regularly work with complex spreadsheets, large Photoshop files, audio projects, video editing or more demanding games, look at a Pro chip. The M5 Pro Mac mini, for example, offers up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU and up to 64GB unified memory.

A Max chip is worth considering for demanding graphics, complex 3D work, high-resolution video production or projects that need more memory than a Pro configuration supports. Many developers, photographers and video editors will be well served by a Pro chip. The M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and up to 128GB unified memory, depending on configuration.

For professional video production, 3D work, software development and other intensive workloads, a Max chip is more appropriate. The Mac Studio with M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and as much as 128GB unified memory. 

The M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU and 512GB unified memory, is aimed at the most extreme workloads, including VFX, scientific computing and running very large AI models locally.

GPU: One of the biggest differences between Apple’s chips is GPU performance. Standard M-series chips are easily sufficient for everyday graphics, casual gaming and light creative work. Pro chips add considerably more GPU power for video editing, graphics work, 3D applications and gaming. Max chips are designed for professional graphics, high-resolution video and demanding 3D workflows, while Ultra provides Apple’s highest GPU performance. The M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores, while the M5 Ultra doubles that to 80 GPU cores. Both also have Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core to speed up AI workloads.

RAM: Apple calls RAM Unified Memory. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB, which is probably the biggest drawback of that machine. Most Macs start with at least 16GB, which is plenty for everyday use, although we recommend choosing more if your budget allows because the memory cannot be upgraded later. 24GB or 32GB is a good choice for heavier multitasking, photo editing, podcasting, moderate video production and gaming. Developers and professional creative users may benefit from 48GB, 64GB or more. The new M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 64GB, M5 Max Mac Studio with up to 128GB, and M5 Ultra Mac Studio with an enormous 512GB.

Storage: Even with iCloud and external drives available, it can seem like you can never have enough storage inside your Mac. 256GB may be sufficient for basic web and office use, but it can fill up quickly. We recommend 512GB for most people who want to keep a Mac for several years, particularly if you store photos, games or media locally. For regular video or audio production, 1TB or more is preferable. Professional users may need several terabytes. The M5 Pro Mac mini offers up to 8TB, while the M5 Ultra Mac Studio and touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro offer up to 16TB. Maximum capacity varies by model and chip, so check the configuration you’re considering. Choose enough internal storage when ordering rather than relying on a later internal upgrade. An external SSD can add capacity for media libraries, project files and archives, often at a lower cost than Apple’s internal storage upgrades.

Display: Consider screen quality and workspace alongside processing power. The MacBook Air’s display is suitable for everyday work and many creative tasks, while MacBook Pro models add XDR brightness and ProMotion refresh rates. The PROLED XDR models also offer OLED, Adobe RGB support and touchscreen input in a lighter design. Choose them if those features will benefit how you work; they use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chip families as the non-touch versions.
